label: Onboarding checklist
summary: An onboarding checklist is a structured set of check items, reminders, and questions that Maaike uses when starting work with a new client or employer. It is organised around role-based collaboration and is aimed specifically at conversation designers. The checklist includes dedicated items for remote onboarding, where the usual informal affordances of office life are absent.
how_maaike_uses: Maaike developed this checklist out of 20+ years of starting new jobs and 4+ years of contracting work, so it reflects hard-won personal experience rather than generic advice. She uses it to get up to speed quickly with new clients, and she pays particular attention to the social side of onboarding: meeting people, building rapport, and navigating the 'black box' of remote work. Two concrete tactics she recommends are a self-organised onboarding tour (scheduling short introductions and asking each person to suggest two more contacts) and a 5 minute online tea break to build informal connection. She also calls on employers and contractors to over-communicate with new remote colleagues, framing the problem in UX terms: without physical affordances, new hires have very little to orient themselves with.
open_questions: The checklist is acknowledged to be incomplete based on Maaike's own experience, so it is an open question which scenarios or roles it does not yet cover.
It is unclear how the checklist changes or should change depending on whether someone is a full-time employee versus a contractor.
